title: Palmerworm, Locust, Cankerworm, Caterpillar
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the Church using Joel's prophecy of the palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, and caterpillar. He argues that these insects represent stages of spiritual decay that have eaten away the original faith and power of the early Church. Branham calls for a return to the original apostolic faith, contending earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.

title: Conference With God
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of having a personal conference with God, using biblical examples such as the conferences in Eden, at the burning bush, at the Red Sea, in Gethsemane, at Calvary, and at Pentecost. He emphasizes that God invites all to reason together and that through faith, believers can receive healing and salvation.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples, such as Nathanael and the Samaritan woman, to show how Jesus revealed His Messiahship through supernatural knowledge, and argues that the same signs should follow believers today.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Divine healing as part of salvation

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the present generation's rejection of the Holy Spirit's work. He emphasizes that unbelief is the original sin and that the sign of the resurrection is available today through the same Holy Spirit that empowered Jesus.

title: The Revelation That Was Given to Me
summary: William Branham recounts his early life, supernatural experiences, and the calling to pray for the sick. He describes visions, an angelic visitation, and the validation of his ministry through healings, emphasizing the unity of believers and the fulfillment of biblical prophecy.

title: And From That Time
subtitle: 60-0210E
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of meeting God, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Peter, Paul, and Bartimaeus. He emphasizes that from the moment one encounters God, life is forever changed, and he demonstrates the presence of Christ through words of knowledge and healing.

title: Hearing, Recognizing, Acting on the Word of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the two spiritual forces represented by Jacob and Esau, emphasizing the difference between the carnal and spiritual believer. He stresses the importance of election, separation from the world, and acting on God's Word, warning against those who come close to the truth but turn away.

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, reflecting on the changes in the valley and the unchanging nature of God. He uses the theme of conferences to illustrate how God calls His people to reason together in times of emergency, citing examples from Eden, the burning bush, the Red Sea, Gethsemane, and Pentecost. He urges the church to hold a conference with God to receive orders and move forward in faith.

title: The Oncoming Storm
summary: William Branham warns of an impending spiritual storm, using the parable of the wise and foolish builders and a story of a Florida hurricane to illustrate the need for preparation. He emphasizes that true safety is found only in Jesus Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, urging listeners to heed the warning before judgment comes.

title: He Careth For You
summary: William Branham preaches on God's care for humanity, emphasizing that only Christ can truly comfort and save. He contrasts worldly substitutes for the Holy Spirit with the genuine comfort found in Jesus, sharing personal testimonies of loss and God's faithfulness.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of encountering God, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Paul, and the woman at the well to illustrate that meeting God changes a person forever. He emphasizes that true conversion is not intellectual but a spiritual experience that leads to a changed life.

title: Former and Latter Rain
summary: William Branham preaches on the end-time signs, comparing the watchman's warning in Zechariah and Isaiah to the present day. He emphasizes the coming of the latter rain and the need for believers to shine as morning stars reflecting Christ's imminent return.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of thirsting for God, using Psalm 63 to emphasize that God's lovingkindness is better than life itself. He shares testimonies of healing, including the story of Florence Nightingale, and calls for unity among believers as sons and daughters of the King.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to recognize Christ's presence in their storms and to have faith in His healing power, demonstrating the gift of discernment as a sign of the Messiah.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God and the need to return to the original Pentecostal experience. He argues that church traditions have perverted the Word of God, and that true faith requires going back to the beginning—to the baptism of the Holy Ghost, divine healing, and the signs and wonders of the early church.

title: Discernment of Spirit
summary: William Branham teaches on the importance of discerning spirits, emphasizing that believers should judge individuals by their motives and objectives rather than by their denomination or outward gifts. He uses Old Testament examples like Moses, Joseph, and David to illustrate how true prophets are anointed by God to glorify Him and edify the Church, not themselves.

title: Why?
summary: In this sermon, William Branham uses the text from Jeremiah 8:20-22 to ask why people refuse God's provided way of salvation and healing. He compares the Holy Spirit to a perfect balm that can heal sin-sick souls, and warns that at the Judgment, God will ask why people rejected His provision. Branham emphasizes that unbelief is the root sin, and that the Holy Spirit is available to all who will receive it.

title: Elijah and the Meal-Offering
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah and the widow of Zarephath, emphasizing faith, sacrifice, and the mixing of the Word and the Spirit. He draws parallels to modern believers, urging them to meet God's requirements and trust in His promises even in dark times.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's faith and belief in God's promise, drawing parallels to the need for faith in divine healing. He emphasizes taking God at His Word without doubting, and highlights the power of the name of Jesus.

title: Door To The Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Jesus stands at the door of the heart and knocks, waiting for individuals to open. He contrasts the honor of receiving earthly dignitaries with the rejection of Christ, and urges listeners to let Jesus be Lord over every area of their lives, including private life, pride, and faith.

title: The Unchangeable God
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God, emphasizing that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples such as Moses, Jacob, Isaiah, and Elijah to illustrate that God works in unexpected ways and times, and calls believers to have faith in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Is There Anything Too Hard For The Lord?
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that nothing is too hard for the Lord, using the story of Abraham and Sarah's visitation by angels in Genesis 18. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a spiritual atmosphere and recognizing God's presence, even when circumstances seem impossible. The sermon includes testimonies of healing and a demonstration of the Holy Spirit's discernment.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite the crowd and distractions. He encourages the audience to cry out for mercy and believe that God has provided a Lamb for their healing and salvation.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the transformative power of encountering God, using the phrase 'from that time' to illustrate how a single moment with God can change a person's life forever. He shares testimonies of biblical figures and modern individuals who were radically changed after meeting God, and calls the congregation to make that decision tonight.

title: Why?
subtitle: 60-0401M
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why people remain sick in sin when God has provided the remedy—the Holy Ghost. He compares the balm in Gilead to a divine toxin that inoculates believers from sin, proven by Christ's life, death, and resurrection.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to seek the Holy Spirit and recognize God's gifts. He emphasizes faith, the supernatural nature of Christianity, and the danger of rejecting divine visitation.

title: As the Eagle Stirreth
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe the Christian life, emphasizing freedom in the Spirit, trust in God's power, and the need to rise above doubt and denominational constraints. He shares personal experiences with eagles to illustrate how believers should rely on God's wings and voice.

title: I Know
subtitle: 60-0417S
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham draws from Job 19:25-27 to emphasize that trials and tribulations are necessary for spiritual growth and to bring believers into a closer fellowship with God. He shares personal experiences of loss and disappointment, testifying that through these 'ash heap' experiences, one can come to the confident declaration, 'I know my Redeemer liveth.' The sermon encourages believers to see beyond present sufferings to the hope of resurrection and the coming of Christ.

title: Go, Tell
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham emphasizes the importance of having a message when we go to tell others about Christ. He contrasts physical preparation with spiritual readiness, urging believers to focus on the resurrection and the power of God rather than on building churches or denominations. The sermon includes baby dedications and a call to believe in the signs that follow believers.

title: The Rejected King
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Israel's demand for a king, drawing parallels to the modern church's tendency to reject the leadership of the Holy Spirit in favor of human leaders and organizations. He emphasizes that God's will is for His people to be led directly by the Spirit, not by men or denominations.

title: Adoption 1
summary: William Branham begins a series on the Book of Ephesians, comparing the believer's journey to Israel's journey from Egypt to Canaan. He emphasizes positional truth in Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit as the promised land for New Testament believers.

title: Adoption 2
summary: William Branham continues a series on the Book of Ephesians, focusing on positional placing of the Church in Christ. He discusses predestination, the manifestation of the sons of God, and the inheritance of believers, drawing parallels between Israel's journey to the Promised Land and the spiritual journey of the Church.

title: Adoption 3
summary: In this lesson, William Branham continues teaching on the Book of Ephesians, focusing on the theme of adoption and positional placing of the church in Christ. He emphasizes that salvation is by grace alone through the Holy Spirit, not by works or denominational affiliation, and calls believers to sanctification and obedience to God's Word.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Adoption 4
summary: William Branham teaches on the mystery of God's will, predestination, and the adoption of sons. He explains that believers are predestined to eternal life and that the church is being prepared as the capstone of the pyramid, perfectly joined to Christ. He emphasizes the coming manifestation of the sons of God and the restoration of man's original dominion.

title: To Whom Shall We Go?
summary: William Branham preaches on the exclusivity of Jesus Christ as the only way, truth, light, foundation, happiness, achievement, and translation to eternal life. He urges listeners to come to Christ rather than rely on creeds, churches, or worldly pursuits.

title: To Whom Would We Go?
summary: William Branham preaches on the uniqueness of Jesus Christ as the only Way, Truth, Light, Foundation, Happiness, Achievement, and Translation. He urges listeners to turn to Christ alone for eternal life and peace, contrasting worldly foundations with the solid rock of Jesus.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the disciples' fear during the storm on the Sea of Galilee and Jesus' reassurance, 'Be not afraid.' He draws parallels to the modern church's drift from the Holy Spirit and calls for a return to prayer, holiness, and reliance on God's power.

title: The Rejected King
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Israel's demand for a king, drawing parallels to modern Christianity's tendency to reject the Holy Spirit's leadership in favor of human organizations and worldly patterns. He warns against denominationalism and emphasizes the need for the Holy Spirit to govern the church.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of Christian fellowship, emphasizing that true fellowship with God and one another is based solely on the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not on organizations, education, or denominations. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle as a type to illustrate the progression from justification through sanctification to the baptism of the Holy Ghost, which brings believers into the Holiest of holies for divine communion.
themes: Justification, sanctification, baptism of the Holy Ghost
The tabernacle as a type of Christ
The super sign of Christ's incarnation

title: Faith Is the Sixth Sense
summary: William Branham teaches that faith is a sixth sense given by God to deliver and rescue us from the limitations of the five physical senses. He argues that this sense has become dormant in many believers due to lack of use and wrong teaching, and he illustrates its power through testimonies of miraculous healings and deliverances.

title: Speak To This Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of speaking to the Rock, which represents Christ, for all needs including salvation, healing, and the Holy Spirit. He uses the Old Testament story of Moses speaking to the rock in the wilderness as a type of Christ, emphasizing that believers today must speak to the Rock in faith. The sermon concludes with a prayer line for the sick.

title: The Unfailing Realities of the Living God
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for true, living religion that brings deliverance, contrasting it with mere creeds and rituals. He emphasizes that God's power is available through the Holy Spirit and the Word, but many reject it because it is too unusual. He calls believers to follow the road map of Scripture without compromise.

title: God's Provided Approach to Divine Fellowship
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of the Blood of Jesus Christ as the only way to restore fellowship between God and man. He uses the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the waters of separation to illustrate how believers must come under the Blood, apply common faith, and enter into the Shekinah Glory of God through the Holy Spirit for true divine fellowship.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a ten-day campaign in Oregon, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the account of Philip bringing Nathanael to Jesus to illustrate that Christ's supernatural knowledge and power are still available today. Branham calls for a soul-stirring revival and urges believers to move with the Spirit rather than settling into denominational complacency.
tags: Jesus Christ same yesterday today forever
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Divine healing through faith in Christ's finished work
The need for revival and moving with the Holy Spirit
The urgency of the Gospel in the end times

title: God's Provided Way of Approach to Fellowship
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of the blood of Jesus Christ as the only way to restore fellowship with God. He uses Old Testament types like the red heifer and the waters of separation to illustrate how faith in Christ's sacrifice cleanses sin and brings believers into communion with God. Branham emphasizes that true fellowship requires both the Word and the Spirit, and that no creed or denomination can substitute for the blood.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba as a type of the last-day church, contrasting her faith with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that the resurrection sign of Jonah is given to this adulterous generation, and that true faith looks away from symptoms to the finished work of Christ.

title: The Door Inside The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ stands at the door of the heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside. He urges believers not only to accept Jesus as Savior but also to let Him be Lord, opening every area of life—including pride and private habits—to His control.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the simplicity of faith, using the story of Blind Bartimaeus and personal anecdotes of healings among Native Americans and in Mexico. He emphasizes that God is the same today as in biblical times and that childlike faith brings healing.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of miracles, including raising a boy from the dead in Finland and healing a crippled girl, emphasizing the power of faith and the importance of a turning point in one's life. He then introduces his sermon 'From That Time' based on Matthew 4:17, discussing how a single moment can change a person's destiny for good or evil.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham closes a revival meeting with thanks, encouragement, and a sermon on Matthew 14:27. He explains the operation of the gift of discernment and healing, emphasizing that faith comes from the people. He shares personal stories and calls for unity and cooperation among believers.

title: It Is I
summary: William Branham speaks on the sign of the Messiah as a prophet, using the story of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' recognition of Him. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Messianic sign of a prophet is still relevant today.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Watchman, What of the Night?
summary: William Branham preaches on the role of the watchman in the Old Testament and applies it to the present day, warning of the approaching judgment and the second coming of Christ. He emphasizes the need for spiritual vigilance and the reflection of Christ's light through the Church in a dark and pleasure-mad world.

title: Speak To The Rock And It Shall Give Forth His Water
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of the Israelites in the wilderness, using the story of Moses striking the rock to bring forth water as a type of the Church's journey to the Promised Land. He emphasizes the importance of faith over carnal thinking, claiming God's promises, and the need for a Spirit-filled church that moves forward despite obstacles.

title: The Unchangeable Word of God
summary: William Branham speaks on the unchanging nature of God's Word, using the Annunciation to Mary as an example of God's faithfulness to His promises. He contrasts the power of God's Word with human traditions and emphasizes the need for signs and wonders in missions.

title: What It Takes To Overcome All Unbelief: Our Faith
summary: William Branham speaks about the universal nature of God's Spirit among believers, the importance of faith over reason, and the need for revival to shake out unbelief. He explains that all redemptive blessings were completed at Calvary and that divine healing is received by faith in God's Word.

title: El-Shaddai
summary: William Branham preaches on God as El-Shaddai, the breasted God who nurses His children back to strength and health. He uses Abraham's story to illustrate total obedience and faith in God's promises, emphasizing that the same Spirit that worked in Christ works in believers today.
themes: The Holy Spirit in the Church

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, emphasizing simple faith and the importance of obedience to God's Word. He shares testimonies of healing among Native Americans and recounts a personal vision of the afterlife, encouraging believers to press on toward the reward.

title: As The Eagle Stirreth Up Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle stirring up its nest to describe how God prepares His children for spiritual growth and freedom. He contrasts the eagle's nature—its ability to soar high, renew its youth, and build its nest on high—with the caged condition of believers bound by creeds and worldliness. Branham calls for a return to the power of the Holy Spirit and the Word, urging believers to rise above earthly limitations.
themes: Eagle as symbol of spiritual life
Renewal of youth through the Holy Spirit
The Word of God as spiritual food
The need for revival and the Holy Spirit

title: Lamb And Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the symbols of the Lamb and the Dove, representing Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the need for believers to be led by the Spirit, bearing fruit rather than manufacturing it, and warns against worldliness in the church.

title: Debate On Tongues
summary: William Branham discusses the gift of speaking in tongues, arguing that it is not the initial evidence of the Holy Spirit. He uses Scripture to show that on the Day of Pentecost, everyone heard in their own language, and that love is the true evidence of the Holy Spirit. He also warns that Satan can counterfeit tongues.
themes: initial evidence of the Holy Spirit
Scripture as the basis of truth
unity of the Body of Christ

title: Five Definite Identifications of the True Church of the Living God
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of the true Church as the mystical Body of Christ, called out from the world and governed by Christ as King. He contrasts this with organized denominations, which he identifies as having an anti-Christ spirit, and emphasizes that the Church is a spiritual kingdom, not a human organization.

title: That Day On Calvary
summary: William Branham preaches on the significance of Calvary, emphasizing that it settled the sin question once for all, broke Satan's power, and opened the way for believers to have eternal life and live selflessly for others. He calls for a genuine, automatic Christian life born of the Spirit, not mere religious works.

title: Visions Of William Branham
summary: William Branham recounts early visions and healings following his ordination, including the healing of a crushed colored man, a crippled Armenian woman, a dying baby, and a paralyzed girl. He emphasizes the importance of waiting for the exact fulfillment of visions and the faithfulness of God's guidance.

title: The Kinsman Redeemer
summary: William Branham preaches on the Book of Ruth, using the story of Ruth and Naomi as a type of the Church and the believer's journey of decision, service, rest, and reward. He emphasizes the concept of the Kinsman Redeemer as a picture of Christ's complete redemption.

title: Condemnation By Representation
summary: William Branham warns against spiritual 'hybreeding'—mixing God's Word with man's theology—which produces a faith without life, unable to reproduce. He traces this from Eve's disobedience to modern denominationalism, urging believers to stay pure to the original Word and Spirit.

title: It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to recognize Christ's presence and power in their lives, especially in times of trouble, and warns against being afraid of the supernatural works of God.

title: Conference
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences with God, using biblical examples such as the Eden conference, the Burning Bush conference, the Red Sea conference, and the Gethsemane conference. He emphasizes that God calls people to reason together and make decisions based on His Word, and that true fellowship with God transforms believers.
themes: the danger of relying on creeds
the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' from Jeremiah 8:20-22, asking why people refuse God's remedy for sin despite His provision. He emphasizes that God has provided a balm in Gilead—the Holy Spirit and new birth—but many reject it due to fear of man or love of sin. Branham calls for repentance and holiness, warning that on Judgment Day God will ask 'Why?' to those who refused His salvation.

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
subtitle: 60-1127M
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of returning to the original Pentecostal experience, warning against hybrid religion that mixes human traditions with God's Word. He emphasizes that God's truth is found at the beginning, not in denominational creeds, and calls believers back to the power and signs of the early church.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham speaks on the Queen of the South, using the biblical account to emphasize the importance of recognizing and receiving God's gifts. He contrasts the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of the Pharisees, and applies the lesson to the present day, urging believers to rally around the gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Revelation of Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham introduces a series on the Seven Church Ages from the Book of Revelation, emphasizing the need for a revelation of Christ in the last days. He discusses the historical and spiritual significance of the church ages, the importance of returning to the Pentecostal experience, and the imminent return of Christ.

title: The Patmos Vision
summary: William Branham begins a series on the Book of Revelation, discussing the five foolish virgins, the remnant, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the importance of revelation knowledge and the unity of God as revealed in Jesus Christ.

title: The Ephesian Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces a series on the seven church ages, beginning with the Ephesian church age. He emphasizes the importance of the Blood tag over denominational brands, and discusses the revelation of Jesus Christ as Almighty God. He outlines the seven church ages and their messengers, and begins to expound on the message to the church at Ephesus.

title: The Smyrnaean Church Age
summary: William Branham teaches on the second church age, Smyrna (A.D. 170-312), a persecuted church that wore the martyr's crown. He identifies Irenaeus as the messenger to this age, emphasizing his stand against organization and for the oneness of God. Branham warns against hybrid religion and urges faithfulness unto death, promising a crown of life to overcomers.

title: The Pergamean Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces the third church age, Pergamos, covering the period from 312 to 606 A.D. He discusses the rise of the Nicolaitane doctrine, the consolidation of church and state under Constantine, and the persecution of true believers. Branham highlights the life and miracles of Saint Martin as a faithful witness during this age, emphasizing the importance of holding fast to the original apostolic faith and the Word of God.

title: The Thyatirean Church Age
summary: William Branham discusses the fourth church age, Thyatira, known as the Dark Age (606-1520 AD). He identifies Columba as the star of this age, a man who rejected Roman doctrine and maintained Pentecostal signs. Branham draws parallels between Jezebel and the Catholic church, warning against spiritual fornication and organizational hierarchy.

title: The Sardisean Church Age
summary: William Branham introduces the fifth church age, Sardis, covering the Reformation period from 1520 to 1750. He discusses the messenger Martin Luther, the deadness of the church, and the remnant that escaped. He also reviews previous church ages and emphasizes the continuity of the Holy Spirit through all ages.

title: The Philadelphian Church Age
summary: William Branham discusses the sixth church age, the Philadelphian Church Age, which he identifies as the age of brotherly love and missionary work, lasting from 1750 to 1906. He highlights John Wesley as the messenger of this age and emphasizes the importance of demonstrating the Gospel through signs and wonders, not just through literature. Branham also shares personal missionary experiences in South Africa to illustrate the power of the Holy Spirit in converting souls.

title: The Ten Virgins, And The Hundred And Forty-Four Thousand Jews
summary: William Branham discusses the end-time events, focusing on the parable of the ten virgins, the sealing of the 144,000 Jews, and the distinction between the Church and Israel. He emphasizes the need for the Holy Spirit baptism and warns against lukewarm Christianity.

title: The Laodicean Church Age
summary: William Branham concludes his series on the seven church ages with the Laodicean age, warning of apostasy and predicting the end of the age by 1977. He discusses the coming Elijah prophet who will restore the faith of the Pentecostal fathers and prepare the church for the Lord's return.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham discusses the uncertainty of the times, drawing from 1 Corinthians 14:8 about the trumpet giving an uncertain sound. He contrasts worldly uncertainty with the certainty of God's Word and the coming of Christ, encouraging faith and preparation for the Rapture.

title: God's Wrapped Gift
summary: In this Christmas sermon, William Branham reflects on the humble birth of Jesus in Bethlehem, emphasizing that God's greatest gift was wrapped in swaddling cloth and laid in a manger. He contrasts the world's rejection of Christ then and now, noting that people refuse the gift because it does not come wrapped in their preferred creeds or societal expectations. Branham calls for a return to the simple, powerful truth of the Gospel and the Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part I
summary: William Branham begins a New Year's Eve service by reflecting on the past year and pressing toward the high calling in Christ. He introduces the fourth chapter of Revelation, explaining that after the Church Age, a door opens in heaven and John is called up to see things to come. Branham emphasizes that Christ is the only door to salvation and warns against rejecting His message.
